In a recent development, furthermore, diversification doesn’t mean guaranteed protection all the time. In 2008, during the global financial crisis, funds built for people retiring in 2010 lost nearly 24% on average.

In principle, savers don’t need to do anything as long as they choose to stay on autopilot until retirement. Fund managers buy and sell assets to stick to the target mix – a practice known as rebalancing.

But rebalancing resets only the broad categories rather than trimming one particular organization for growing too large. As Nvidia’s share of the market rose, so did its share of the fund.

For people who hold just one target-date fund, I believe the right response to this month’s news is to leave their 401(k) account alone. The fund has been rebalancing all along, and your stake in any one firm is modest.

But a saver still needs to check three things.

First, consider the year you expect to retire. If you want to move it earlier or later, or want more or less risk, you should choose a fund with a different year.

Second, look at what the fund’s share of stocks is today, which is on the fund’s fact sheet. If you’re 60 and your fund is 60% stocks, a 30% fall in stocks would cut your balance by roughly 18%. If that would derail your retirement plans, you can switch to an earlier-dated fund that holds less in stocks and brings less risk.

Third, if you have other funds, you should review them. About 1 in 4 target-date investors in Vanguard plans hold other funds. If you add a tech fund or an S&P 500 fund, your account is riskier and more concentrated than the label suggests.

About 31% of savers in Vanguard plans opt out of target-date funds and choose their own investments, perhaps because they find target-date funds too conservative or their fees too costly. For these investors, and for anyone with old 401(k)s and IRAs, there is more to do.

Start by looking at the fact sheet for each fund, like this one for Vanguard’s S&P 500 index fund, and compare the top holdings. An S&P 500 index fund, a large-cap growth fund and a technology or Nasdaq-tracking fund look like three investments. But in fact you may own the same handful of companies three times.

In a recent development, next, you should rebalance your holdings according to your plan, not to a prediction. That means returning to the mix of stocks and bonds that you chose in the first place. Trades inside a 401(k) don’t trigger taxes, and many aims offer automatic rebalancing. If yours doesn’t, a simple rule backed by Vanguard research works: review once or twice a year, and rebalance whenever any part of your mix drifts more than about 5 percentage points from your target.

Finally, consider broadening the stocks you own. Morningstar Indexes strategist Dan Lefkovitz has pointed to U.S. value stocks, smaller companies and international stocks as areas with less AI exposure. Your blueprint may offer funds for each.

According to recent reports, none of these makes you immune to losses, and diversifying can mean trailing the hottest part of the market for years. But the pattern can flip promptly: International stocks gained about 29% in 2025, far ahead of the S&P 500’s 16%.

How much this month’s news matters depends on when you’ll need the money.

Industry observers note that if you’re decades from retirement, a downturn can work in your favor, because every paycheck contribution buys shares at lower prices. Keep contributing and capture your full employer match. My own research with a colleague has found that accounts on systematic investment prepares akin to 401(k)s earned better market-adjusted returns than accounts funded with lump sums.

It has been revealed that if you’re within 5-10 years of retirement, the bigger danger is what planners call sequence-of-returns risk: A large loss right before or just after you start withdrawing can permanently shrink what your savings can support. A good defense is to hold several years of expected withdrawals in lower-risk assets, such as bonds or money market funds, so you’re never forced to sell stocks after a drop. For retirees, Morningstar’s Christine Benz suggests one to two years of withdrawals in cash and five to eight more in bonds.

The costliest mistake is usually the most tempting: selling everything and waiting for the dust to settle.

According to recent reports, during the 2008-09 financial crisis, about 117,000 Fidelity 401(k) participants moved entirely out of stocks. Those who stayed out saw their balances grow just 2% by mid-2011, while those who kept some stock exposure saw balances rise 50% on average.

Other moves to avoid include stopping your own 401(k) contributions, chasing whatever theme looks safe this month, and pulling money out early, which can mean taxes, penalties and a locked-in loss.

Last, don’t hand the decision to a chatbot. It will likely give you sound general guidance, such as diversifying and not panic-selling, and that consensus advice is where AI is reliable. But it is weakest on high-stakes questions that turn on your own situation.

Recent findings suggest that this story was updated on Nov. 23, 2006, to note Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia’s CEO and the rebound in the firm’s share price.

Pawan Jain is a professor of finance at Texas A&M University.

Anthropic is rolling out a newly introduced Claude app for Android that picks up a Material 3 Expressive redesign.

Confirmed on Twitter/X by Anthropic Product Manager Robert Bye, Claude is now rolling out a Material 3 Expressive redesign for its Android app that, while not a full embrace of Google’s design language, does make a clear attempt to better fit in on Android.

The updated design picks up a bottom-bar UI as opposed to relying fully on the old hamburger menu – it still exists, but it’s mainly for chat history now. You can see M3 elements throughout the app, including in the model switcher and the background of chats. It’s clearly themed to match Anthropic’s aesthetic, and there’s no obvious implementation of Material You colors, but it all fits within the general Material 3 guidelines – much more so than the original app.

The one flaw we spotted was the predictive back implementation, which gets a neat animation to move the search bar but is supposed to show a preview of the previous screen, but that’s just nit-picking, really.

The new Claude app for Android is rolling out now.

Breaking: Open-source DeepResearch – Freeing our search agents

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, yesterday, OpenAI released Deep Research, a system that browses the web to summarize content and answer questions based on the summary.
  • One of the main results in the blog post is a strong improvement of performances on the General AI Assistants benchmark (GAIA), a benchmark we’ve been playing with recently as well, where they successfully reached near 67% correct answers on 1-shot on average, and 47.6% on especially challenging “level 3” questions that involve multiple steps of reasoning and tool usage (see below for a presentation of GAIA).
  • DeepResearch is composed of an LLM (which can be selected from the current list of LLMs provided by OpenAI, 4o, o1, o3, etc) and an internal “agentic framework” which guide the LLM to use tools like web search and organize its actions in steps.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, yesterday, OpenAI released Deep Research, a system that browses the web to summarize content and answer questions based on the summary. The system is impressive and blew our minds when we tried it for the first time.

One of the main results in the blog post is a strong improvement of performances on the General AI Assistants benchmark (GAIA), a benchmark we’ve been playing with recently as well, where they successfully reached near 67% correct answers on 1-shot on average, and 47.6% on especially challenging “level 3” questions that involve multiple steps of reasoning and tool usage (see below for a presentation of GAIA).

DeepResearch is composed of an LLM (which can be selected from the current list of LLMs provided by OpenAI, 4o, o1, o3, etc) and an internal “agentic framework” which guide the LLM to use tools like web search and organize its actions in steps.

In a recent development, while powerful LLMs are now freely available in open-source (see e.g. the recent DeepSeek R1 model), OpenAI didn’t disclose much about the agentic framework underlying Deep Research….

So we decided to embark on a 24-hour mission to reproduce their results and open-source the needed framework along the way!

In a recent development, the clock is ticking, let’s go! ⏱️.

It has been revealed that almost everyone has already experienced how powerful LLMs can be simply by playing with chatbots.. However, what not everyone is aware of yet is that integrating these LLMs into agentic systems can give them real superpowers!

Here is a recent example comparing the performance of a few frontier LLMs with and without an agentic framework (in this case the simple smolagents library) - using an agentic framework bumps performance by up to 60 points!

In fact, OpenAI also highlighted in its release blogpost how Deep Research performed dramatically better than standalone LLMs on the knowledge-intensive "Humanity’s Last Exam" benchmark.

So, what happens when we integrate our current top LLM in an agentic framework, to work toward an open-DeepResearch ?

It has been revealed that A quick note: We’ll benchmark our results on the same GAIA challenge but keep in mind that this is a work in progress. DeepResearch is a massive achievement and its open reproduction will take time. In particular, full parity will require improved browser use and interaction like OpenAI Operator is providing, i.e. beyond the current text-only web interaction we explore in this first step.

Let’s first understand the scope of the challenge: GAIA.

GAIA is arguably the most comprehensive benchmark for agents. Its questions are very difficult and hit on many challenges of LLM-based systems. Here is an example of a hard question:.

It has been revealed that which of the fruits shown in the 2008 painting "Embroidery from Uzbekistan" were served as part of the October 1949 breakfast menu for the ocean liner that was later used as a floating prop for the film "The Last Voyage"? Give the items as a comma-separated list, ordering them in clockwise order based on their arrangement in the painting starting from the 12 o'clock position. Use the plural form of each fruit.

You can see this question involves several challenges:.

Solving this requires both high-level planning abilities and rigorous execution, which are two areas where LLMs struggle when used alone.

So it’s an excellent test set for agent systems!

According to recent reports, on GAIA’s public leaderboard, GPT-4 does not even reach 7% on the validation set when used without any agentic setup. On the other side of the spectrum, with Deep Research, OpenAI reached 67.36% score on the validation set, so an order of magnitude better! (Though we don’t know how they would actually fare on the private test set.).

Let’s see if we can do better with open source tools!

The first improvement over traditional AI agent systems we’ll tackle is to use a so-called “code agent”. As shown by Wang et al. (2024), letting the agent express its actions in code has several advantages, but most notably that code is specifically designed to express complex sequences of actions.

Consider this example given by Wang et al.:.

This highlights several advantages of using code:.

The advantages above were confirmed by our experiments on the agent_reasoning_benchmark.

From building smolagents we can also cite a notable additional advantage, which is a better handling of state: this is very useful for multimodal tasks in particular. Need to store this image/audio/other for later use? No problem, just assign it as a variable in your state and you can re-use it 4 steps later if needed. In JSON you would have to let the LLM name it in a dictionary key and trust the LLM will later understand that it can still use it.

Now we need to provide the agent with the right set of tools.

It has been revealed that 1. A web browser. While a fully fledged web browser interaction like Operator will be needed to reach full performance, we started with an extremely simple text-based web browser for now for our first proof-of-concept. You can find the code here.

2. A simple text inspector, to be able to read a bunch of text file format, find it here.

It has been revealed that these tools were taken from the excellent Magentic-One agent by Microsoft Research, kudos to them! We didn’t change them much, as our goal was to get as high a performance as we can with the lowest complexity possible.

Here is a short roadmap of improvements which we feel would really improve these tools’ performance (feel free to open a PR and contribute!):.

In our 24h+ reproduction sprint, we’ve already seen steady improvements in the performance of our agent on GAIA!

We’ve quickly gone up from the previous SoTA with an open framework, around 46% for Magentic-One, to our current performance of 55.15% on the validation set.

Recent findings suggest that this bump in performance is due mostly to letting our agents write their actions in code! Indeed, when switching to a standard agent that writes actions in JSON instead of code, performance of the same setup is instantly degraded to 33% average on the validation set.

Here is the final agentic system.

We’ve set up a live demo here for you to try it out!

According to recent reports, however, this is only the beginning, and there are a lot of things to improve! Our open tools can be made better, the smolagents framework can also be tuned, and we’d love to explore the performance of better open models to support the agent.

According to recent reports, we welcome the community to come join us in this endeavour, so we can leverage the power of open research together to build a great open-source agentic framework! It would allow anyone to run a DeepResearch-like agent at home, with their favorite models, using a completely local and customized approach!

While we were working on this and focusing on GAIA, other great open implementations of Deep Research emerged from the community, specifically from.

Recent findings suggest that each of these implementations use different libraries for indexing data, browsing the web and querying LLMs. In this project, we would like to reproduce the benchmarks presented by OpenAI (pass@1 average score), benchmark and document our findings with switching to open LLMs (like DeepSeek R1), using vision LMs, benchmark traditional tool calling against code-native agents.

OpenAI’s Deep Research is probably boosted by the excellent web browser that they introduced with Operator.

So we’re tackling that next! In a more general problem: we’re going to build GUI agents, i.e. “agents that view your screen and can act directly with mouse & keyboard”. If you’re excited about this project, and want to help everyone get access to such cool capabilities through open source, we’d love to get your contribution!

We’re also hiring a full time engineer to help us work on this and more, apply if you’re interested 🙂.

Travis and Jason Kelce’s Garage Beer lands $20 million as craft brewers pull back

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1673 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that travis Kelce’s beer brand just secured a huge financial deal to help promote its popular brew.
  • Industry observers note that travis Kelce’s beer brand just secured a huge financial deal to help promote its popular brew.
  • The funding comes at a time when the independent beer industry has been facing many challenges.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that travis Kelce’s beer brand just secured a huge financial deal to help promote its popular brew. On Tuesday, Travis and his brother Jason Kelce’s Garage Beer brand secured a $20 million revolving credit from Tiger Finance, according to a release. The funding comes at a time when the independent beer industry has been facing many challenges. The rise in operation costs, slowing business openings, and declines in sales have forced many breweries to close down or refinance. But this celebrity-backed brand is only seeing success. Andy Cerussi, the senior managing director of Tiger Finance, remarked in the release that the manufacturer is thrilled to have been chosen as the preferred financial partner, saying that the company is “impressed with [the] impact the Kelce brothers have had on positively influencing brand awareness.” Brian Amicon, president of Garage Beer, told Inc. that as the company continues to grow, this financing allows it greater flexibility. “From strengthening our distribution to investing in the brand and creating more opportunities to connect with consumers, it puts us in a strong position to keep building what we’ve started,” Amicon said. “We’re proud of the progress we’ve made and excited to keep pushing forward.” A $20 million bet on Garage Beer’s brand strength The debt deal allows Garage Beer to expand its product line and enter new markets. At $20 million, the financing sits on the smaller side of the funding spectrum—in the bottom quarter of deals tracked, according to Deal Room. But for a consumer company like a beer line, debt against brand strength gives growth capital without diluting equity. This revolving line will give Garage Beer flexible access to capital tied to its brand value. The Columbus, Ohio-based brand originally released as a local craft light lager by Braxton Brewing Co., but was spun off into an independent company in 2023 by its CEO, Andy Sauer. According to VinePair, the Kelce brothers joined Garage Beer in the summer of 2024 by acquiring a majority stake and becoming co-owners and operators. This move rapidly boosted the brand’s national visibility. In late 2025, Durational Capital Management confirmed its strategic investment partnership with the company. A cofounder of Durational Capital said in the release that the company appreciates Tiger’s creativity and partnership “to structure a credit facility that leverages the strength of Garage Beer’s brand to support the company’s growth objectives.” Garage Beer is expanding while competitors retrench Neil Reid, a professor at the University of Toledo who studies the craft beer industry, told Inc. that the brand’s trajectory stands out. “Garage Beer’s aggressive expansion is highly unusual in today’s beer market,” Reid said. He noted that the company has expanded distribution to all 50 states and added more than 100,000 barrels of volume in 2025, reportedly the largest increase among U.S. craft brewers. “Rather than retrenching, Garage Beer is using the downturn to gain market share from competitors,” Reid told Inc. He added that brands with the capacity for growth through distribution often tend to be a simple product and have broad appeal, sales momentum, enough capital to fund expansion, name recognition, and scalable operations. It has been revealed that he noted that the tech giant has expanded distribution to all 50 states and added more than 100,000 barrels of volume in 2025, reportedly the largest increase among U.S. craft brewers.

Southwest Airlines is offering 55 days of buy-one-get-one flights. Here’s how to get them

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1089 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Southwest Airlines is taking a slightly different approach to Black Friday this year.
  • Recent findings suggest that southwest Airlines is taking a slightly different approach to Black Friday this year.
  • On Friday, Southwest announced a three-day promotion that allows Rapid Rewards members to earn a temporary Companion Pass by booking and completing just one round-trip flight or two one-way flights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Southwest Airlines is taking a slightly different approach to Black Friday this year. Rather than simply discounting flights, the airline is giving travelers an opportunity to earn one of its most coveted perks: the Companion Pass. On Friday, Southwest announced a three-day promotion that allows Rapid Rewards members to earn a temporary Companion Pass by booking and completing just one round-trip flight or two one-way flights. The offer comes just weeks before Southwest is set to overhaul its Rapid Rewards loyalty program, significantly changing how travelers qualify for the benefit. How to earn Southwest’s promotional Companion Pass If you’re already planning to fly over the holidays, earning the pass could be relatively easy. To take advantage of the promotion, travelers will need to: Register for the promotion through Southwest. Book eligible flights between November 27 and November 29. Complete either a single round-trip flight or two one-way flights between November 27 and January 5, 2027. Travelers who score the pass will be able to bring a designated companion on eligible flights between January 8 and March 3, 2027 for free, with the exception of taxes and fees, which start at $5.60 each way. There’s also no limit to the number of eligible flights travelers can use the pass for during the promotional period, so you and your companion could, in theory, go on a 2-month adventure only paying for one of your flights. Southwest is changing how travelers earn a Companion Pass The promotion comes at an interesting time for Southwest. In October, the airline unveiled changes to its Rapid Rewards loyalty program that will take effect on January 1, 2027. Under the existing program, travelers can earn a Companion Pass by completing 100 qualifying one-way flights or accumulating 135,000 Companion Pass qualifying points in a calendar year. Starting in January, Southwest will eliminate Companion Pass qualifying points and instead use Tier Qualifying Points to determine eligibility for elite status and Companion Pass benefits. The airline is also introducing a upcoming milestone reward that gives members three Companion Pass trips, while travelers who reach its new Platinum elite status will receive unlimited companion trips. One of the biggest changes is how credit card rewards factor into the equation. Historically, Southwest credit card welcome bonuses have offered a particularly lucrative shortcut to earning a Companion Pass. Starting in 2027, those bonuses will no longer count toward qualification. The same goes for referral bonuses, anniversary points, and points earned through hotel and rental car partners. Everyday spending on Southwest credit cards will still help travelers qualify, with cardholders earning one Tier Qualifying Point per dollar spent. There’s still time to earn a Companion Pass under the old rules Southwest is giving prospective credit card customers one final opportunity to take advantage of the existing qualification structure. Travelers who apply for a Southwest Rapid Rewards credit card by December 14, are approved, and meet the spending requirements for its welcome bonus can still have those bonus points count toward earning a Companion Pass under the 2026 rules, even if they complete the spending requirement in early 2027. Those who meet the overall qualification requirements can enjoy unlimited companion flights through December 31, 2027. For travelers who don’t fly Southwest often enough to qualify for the traditional Companion Pass, however, this weekend’s Black Friday promotion offers a much easier way to experience the perk, even if only for a couple of months.

Hands-on: Baseus’ fresh PicoGo Pro USB-C charger is clever, cute, and on sale

💡 Key Takeaways
  • USB-C chargers are pretty standardized at this point, but there’s a fun newly introduced trend of adding displays to your power brick that I’ve been very much enjoying, and the new PicoGo Pro from Baseus is a great example with three ports, optimized charging, and a cute little character to top it off – and for Black Friday, it’s pretty deeply discounted, too.
  • It has been revealed that the Baseus PicoGo Pro (AH22) is a 100W, 3-port USB-C charger designed to top off your laptop, phone, and/or tablet, even all at the same time.
  • Using GaN tech, PicoGo Pro is very compact at about 2 inches tall and a little over an inch wide.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

USB-C chargers are pretty standardized at this point, but there’s a fun newly introduced trend of adding displays to your power brick that I’ve been very much enjoying, and the new PicoGo Pro from Baseus is a great example with three ports, optimized charging, and a cute little character to top it off – and for Black Friday, it’s pretty deeply discounted, too.

It has been revealed that the Baseus PicoGo Pro (AH22) is a 100W, 3-port USB-C charger designed to top off your laptop, phone, and/or tablet, even all at the same time. For anyone who travels often or just has a lot of devices on hand, chargers like this are a must. Having something you don’t have to think twice about when it comes to charging rates is just so nice, and these have come a long way, too.

Using GaN tech, PicoGo Pro is very compact at about 2 inches tall and a little over an inch wide. I remember having single-port chargers that could barely fast-charge my phone that were twice this size just a few years ago. GaN just absolutely rules, and Baseus is using a special version that reduces heat and improves efficiency.

But the two reasons I really like this charger aren’t strictly to do with GaN.

Recent findings suggest that the first is the built-in display. Again, that’s a trend throughout the industry. Anker has several chargers out with built-in displays as the firm helped to really make this popular – the Anker Prime 160W brick is really similar to PicoGo Pro (at a higher price), and it’s the only I’ve been using for months before trying out this Baseus model.

Baseus has a cute little animated character that accompanies your charging, with little eyes when the charger isn’t active and some fun animations to show your charging rate in real-time. Neat! You can “press” the button to move through the UI and even see the specific charging rate of each connected device. You’ll also see that the brick can recognize the device you have plugged in, though Android devices just show a generic “SAMSUNG” or whatever brand you plug in – Anker, again, had a similar set of features in a brick released earlier in 2026, but some of those features were iPhone-only, and that brick was only a 1-port, 45W charger anyway.

According to recent reports, but, like that Anker brick, Baseus supports “smart” charging that adjusts to your device. Plugging in a Galaxy Z Fold 8 that was around 65% full, I saw the brick adjust its charging speed to tailor to the phone, initially going up to full speed before settling down around 28W~. You can manually adjust this with “Turbo” or “Gentle” modes, the former maxing out the charging rate and the latter settling in around 15W for a slower charge. That flexibility is great because it means you can adjust the charging rate to what you need in that moment. Full-speed for a quick top-off on a busy day, slower charging overnight to preserve battery health.

Baseus isn’t doing much newly introduced here, though the GaN tech mentioned earlier is enhanced by some architecture and algorithm adjustments the company has made behind the scenes, but it’s a really good implementation.

Beyond that, it’s also priced pretty well.

Industry observers note that baseus PicoGo Pro’s full price is $59.99, but you’ll probably rarely see it there. Technically, today is its launch date, and it’s already down by over 30% at $39.70 for Black Friday. Value-wise, this one is hard to beat.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the people at Sony don’t use words like “product” or “reboot” when they talk about Aibo, the Japanese electronics and entertainment tech giant’s robotic dog.Aibo robots, which first went on sale in 1999, are all sold out and no longer in production.
  • The people at Sony don’t use words like “product” or “reboot” when they talk about Aibo, the Japanese electronics and entertainment manufacturer’s robotic dog.Aibo robots, which first went on sale in 1999, are all sold out and no longer in production.
  • Yuri Kageyama is on Threads: https://www.threads.com/@yurikageyama.

According to recent reports, the people at Sony don’t use words like “product” or “reboot” when they talk about Aibo, the Japanese electronics and entertainment tech giant’s robotic dog.Aibo robots, which first went on sale in 1999, are all sold out and no longer in production. But some owners who had to part with their Aibo have donated the robots to Tokyo-based Sony Group Corp. for an “adoption program,” where they get treated to repairs and upgrades.Those robot pets now have new homes in hospitals and other facilities, bringing solace and smiles to patients and staff.Sony does not disclose the pricing or the number of Aibo robots that have been sold.Packed with sensors, digital cameras and an intelligence of sorts, Aibo has been programmed to remember its name, the owner’s face and its surroundings — details of everyday life that make for a disarming illusion of a personality.The robot barks, cocks its head, moves its ears, waddles toward you, acts happy when petted and goes to “sleep” — in short it simulates a puppy, except this one can take snapshots and monitors its own mechanical dysfunctions.“The owners feel as though they are sending off what has become to them like their own child,” remarked Sony official Yoshiyuki Katsuno, who oversees the program.Aibo gets people talking to each other, and can offer tired souls a perk to pick themselves up and keep going, according to Katsuno.“We hope to spread the emotional healing and human interaction that Aibo has to offer,” he said.At the St. Marianna University School of Medicine in Kawasaki, on the outskirts of Tokyo, a nurse had to do some looking to find a wandering Aibo during a recent visit.But Aibo has helped with the long waits for visiting patients and succeeded in persuading reluctant children to get examined, claims Dr. Manabu Komori of the department of otolaryngology.That field involves diagnosing and treating sicknesses related to the ear, nose and throat, with many child patients.“It helps motivate the kids,” Komori said. “Going to a hospital is basically not very pleasant.”The hospital also uses real dogs to help patients feel better, though the animals require care and food and can be temperamental. That means a robot dog offers some advantages, although Komori was careful not to say they were better than real dogs.Cuteness is seen as desirable in Japanese culture, where being “kawaii,” or “cute,” is not a sign of weakness or inferiority, but an endearing trait that encourages harmony and communication — both valued in Japanese society.And so, if the need is for a soulmate, it’s better to have that cute look, be it a dog, cat or even a duck, said Jerry Wang, Executive Chairman of FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem, a U.S. company that offers more foreboding-looking four-legged patrol robots.“If you want some emotional attachment, you want a cute shape,” he said. A short clip can help a project in different ways. It can show an idea you have not filmed, put an existing design in motion, or give an announcement something to look at. The same approach will not work if the clip needs to demonstrate a real feature or show exactly what happened. Before choosing a generator, decide what the viewer needs to learn from the shot.

This article uses Kling 4.0 as a worked example, but the decision process applies to any AI video generator. It covers how these tools turn prompts and images into video, how Kling 4.0 and a few alternatives differ, how to choose a starting mode, how to add exact text and branding outside the generated clip with a short ffmpeg script, and when real footage is the better choice. Feature details come from each vendor’s own pages at the time of writing and change often, so confirm current terms before you proposal a production.

Sources indicate that ● Generated video is best for imagined shots. It suits concepts, backgrounds and early explorations, not instructions or faithful records.

● Your starting material decides the mode. A written idea, a reference image or a pair of opening and closing frames each call for a different input.

● Keep exact wording out of the generated clip. Titles, dates and logos belong on separate layers in an editor.

● Tools differ on control, cost and licensing. Compare inputs, length, resolution, credits and terms before you commit.

According to recent reports, ● Always review. Watch the whole clip at its final size and check it against the real product or design.

Sources indicate that most current systems extend diffusion models across time. A model learns to turn noise into a coherent set of frames guided by a prompt, and sometimes by an image or a clip. The research paper Video Diffusion Models describes this extension from images to video. The practical consequences are easy to observe.

● The prompt describes change over time. One visible change and one camera instruction usually work better than a long list of actions.

According to recent reports, ● Reference material steers but does not lock. A picture can suggest shape and colour without guaranteeing an exact match.

Industry observers note that ● Longer clips give more room for drift. Faces, logos and fine text are the first things to change between frames.

Industry observers note that ● Cost grows with length and resolution. Most hosted tools charge credits per second, so short previews are cheaper than full shots.

If you only have an idea, start with text. For a short announcement, you might ask for a band of light to move across a wall of coloured tiles. No one needs to recognise a particular wall, so the model can decide how it looks. Give it one visible change and a clear view of the subject. A prompt such as Soft morning light travels slowly across a wall of blue ceramic tiles. Fixed camera, no lettering is enough to see whether the idea works.

If you already have an illustration or a photo, reference mode gives you another starting point. Suppose you want a short concept clip for a desk accessory that only exists as a drawing. The picture can show the general shape and colour while the prompt describes the view you want. A video reference can help when it is the motion that is hard to explain, such as a slow camera slide. Say what each asset is meant to guide, and do not add a clip just because you have one.

Use keyframes when a particular view matters at a particular moment. Start with an opening image. If a short reveal also needs to end with the object facing forward, add an ending image to show that view. That is different from a reference image that mainly shows what the object looks like. Neither method guarantees an exact match, so check the result rather than assuming the uploaded picture has locked the design.

Sources indicate that no single tool fits every project. The table summarizes what each option’s own page states, and “not stated” means the page did not say, not that the feature is absent.

According to recent reports, reading the table: hosted studios such as the one on JXP are the quickest way to test an idea and need no setup, but you pay per second and work within their supported inputs. Kling’s own site is the place to check announcements and API options directly, since its page notes little about durations or resolution. Runway positions its models for motion quality and prompt following, while Google’s Gemini API video documentation suits teams building generation into their own products. The Diffusers video guide covers open-source pipelines for developers who want local control and are ready to manage GPUs and licences.

Trying an idea before making it. An illustrator might want to see how an imagined landscape feels when the light changes. A quick clip gives the team something to discuss: is the change visible, and does it happen at the right pace? It does not need to be the final animation to answer those questions.

Showing a product concept. A rotating view or a slow camera move can help people discuss how a design might be presented. It is useful early, when the shape and lighting are still being explored. Once the clip represents a product someone can buy, the standard changes. If a port moves or a button appears that the real product does not have, it is the wrong clip for that job.

According to recent reports, making a short visual for a post. A few seconds of moving colour can give an event announcement or a project update a distinctive opening. Put the name, date and other exact wording in your editor so they are readable and easy to change. The background only needs to support the message. If it competes with the text, use less movement or keep the background still.

Industry observers note that generated video is unreliable at lettering, so add titles in an editor or with a script. The command below overlays a title on a generated background and then checks the file properties. It assumes you already have a clip named background.mp4 and ffmpeg installed.

-vf "drawtext=text='Launch Night | 12 March':fontcolor=white:fontsize=64:x=(w-text_w)/2:y=(h-text_h)/2:box=1:boxcolor=black@0.35:boxborderw=24" \.

-c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -an announcement.mp4.

ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 \.

-show_entries stream=width,height,r_frame_rate,duration \.

-of default=noprint_wrappers=1 announcement.mp4.

According to recent reports, because the text lives in the command, you can reuse the same background for three events by changing one string. The font may need to be set with a fontfile option on some systems. This is the practical version of keeping the moving background in one file and the editable details in another.

Sources indicate that if people will follow the clip as instructions, use real footage or a screen recording for the steps. A convincing shot of an app is not proof that a button is in the right place. A generated close-up of a product is not a reliable way to show how its parts fit. You can still use an imagined opening, but make the switch to the real demonstration clear.

Think about revisions, too. If your team expects to adjust the same title, logo or date every week, put those elements on separate layers in an editor. And if the only movement you need is a slow zoom on an approved picture, apply that zoom directly. There is no reason to risk changing the picture when a simple edit will do.

This matters when someone else will maintain the video. A reusable announcement template is easier to hand over if the moving background is one file and the event details are editable. If the team likes the movement but needs three versions with different dates, they can reuse the same clip. If every change calls for a fresh generation, the time you saved on the first version may disappear on the second.

The Kling 4.0 video generator on JXP currently offers 720p and 1080p settings and clip lengths from 3 to 30 seconds. According to its page, reference mode accepts up to 10 images and 5 videos, keyframe mode takes a first frame, middle frames and an optional last frame, and credits are charged per second with a higher rate at 1080p. For a first attempt, choose the frame shape you initiative to use and make the clip only as long as it needs to be. Check the displayed credit cost before generating, because a short preview can tell you whether the direction works before you spend on a longer shot.

Recent findings suggest that decide what a good result looks like before you generate it. For the tile background, you need to see the light move without distracting from the words you will add. For a product concept, check whether the shape stays recognisable as the viewpoint changes. Watch the whole clip at the size the audience will see it. If the shot misses the point, revise one thing at a time: the motion, the framing or the source image.

Recent findings suggest that ● Read the licence. JXP’s page lists a commercial use license on each initiative and indicates outputs are for creative and lawful use, with the user responsible for reviewing them. Other tools have different terms.

● Do not misrepresent products or events. A generated clip should not suggest features or footage that do not exist.

● Consider provenance. C2PA is an open standard for Content Credentials that records where content came from and how it was edited, and some tools support it.

Sources indicate that ● Disclose where required. Follow platform and advertising rules on labelling AI-generated or altered content.

● Fine text, logos, hands and fast motion can drift or flicker between frames.

● Reference images and keyframes steer the result but do not guarantee an exact match.

● Vendor specifications, such as resolution and length, can differ between a model announcement and a particular platform.

● Credit costs and plan terms change, so check them on the day you generate.

● Long or exact sequences are often cheaper and safer to film than to generate.

Short imagined shots, concept clips and moving backgrounds, where some details can be left open and the clip is reviewed before use.

Use text when you only have an idea, reference mode when you have a picture or clip to guide the look, and keyframes when specific views matter at specific moments.

Industry observers note that not reliably. Use real footage or a screen recording for instructions and demonstrations.

Sources indicate that no. Hosted studios, vendor sites, developer APIs and open-source pipelines all exist. Compare supported inputs, length, resolution, cost and licensing against your project.

In a recent development, kling 4.0 is a good candidate when the missing piece is an imagined shot and you can describe what it needs to do. Pick one such shot, try it, and put it next to the material you already have, and compare at least one alternative before you commit. If the project needs exact instructions or a faithful record, use the real thing. A useful first result is one that does its job in the edit, not simply one that looks impressive on its own.

Recent findings suggest that HP's Omen prebuilt PC comes in a standard mid-tower size, but crams in an RTX 5070 GPU, 32GB of DDR5-6000 memory, and an Intel Core Ultra 7 265F. Boasting a steep 38% discount at HP for Black Friday, this system offers mid-range specs at a comfortable mid-range price. One thing to note about HP's modern prebuilt desktops is that, unlike the days of yore, they actually use standardized parts, meaning that upgrading the system later down the line (perhaps when PC component pricing calms down), you'll be all set to upgrade without the hassle of having to work around proprietary boards and parts.

Alongside the CPU GPU, and RAM, you also get a 1TB PCIe Gen 4 drive for all of the games you'll download onto the system, and there's also a spare slot, in case you want to expand the capacity in the future, and whenever the price of RAM comes down, you might also wish to populate the two empty DIMM slots over on the motherboard.

Get an RTX 5070-powered PC, paired with an Intel Core Ultra 7 265F, 32GB of Kingston Fury DDR5-6000 RAM, and a 1TB SSD; the system also offers plenty of space to upgrade storage and memory capacities in the future. Expect a solid mid-tower chassis with an 850W power supply and an Intel B860 chipset motherboard.

Intel has not specified the make or manufacturer of the B860 motherboard contained within the system, but we do get further details about its I/O and connectivity options. Expect a Realtek connectivity chipset with support for WI-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.3 for all your controllers and peripherals, alongside a host of ports, including 2x USB-C 10Gbps, 4x USB-A ports at 5Gbps, and a further 4x USB-A 2.0 ports.

According to recent reports, the entire system makes for a solid 1440p-focused build, and with the RTX 5070 paired nicely with Intel's Core Ultra 7 265KF, the 20-core CPU, consisting of 8 P-cores and 12 E-cores, will perform nicely, with boost clocks at up to 5.4GHz on the P-cores. Therefore, our mystery unspecified motherboard will be running LGA 1851, which is running towards its end of life. So, while other aspects of the system remain fairly upgradable, do be aware that if you want a CPU upgrade, drop-in options will be limited without having to switch platforms to Nova Lake or other future architectures. Despite this, you can't refute a good offer, and armed with a staggering $1400 off its current MSRP at HP for Black Friday, it still offers heaps of value in the current climate.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that your kid is becoming quite the capitalist. Every U.S. child with an active Trump account will soon receive two shares of SpaceX, the space exploration manufacturer run by Elon Musk. This donation marks the latest in a string of philanthropic initiatives focused on these new types of tax-advantaged investment accounts. SpaceX announced Wednesday that the company will donate one share of its Class A common stock—currently trading for more than $130 per share—to every currently active Trump account. In turn, CEO Musk will match that donation, which he later confirmed on X. “Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally,” Musk posted. In its official announcement, SpaceX touted its future-focused mission of building new infrastructure that could achieve multiplanetary living. “We believe ownership of the company creating these systems should extend to the next generation of Americans for their long-term benefit.” Here’s what we know about the donations. MILLIONS OF NEW SHAREHOLDERS The portfolios of the country’s youngest generation of investors keep getting fatter. Released earlier this year, Trump accounts allow deposits of up to $5,000 per year for each child until the age of 18 and various billionaires have even thrown some money into the mix. Musk now joins the likes of Michael Dell and Ray Dalio, who have similarly pledged donations to Trump accounts. The U.S. Treasury Department, too, will make a one-time $1,000 deposit to every child born between Jan. 1, 2025, and Dec. 31, 2028. The SpaceX shares work a little differently in that the company will transfer one share of its stock to active Trump accounts in December, according to Musk’s post. Nearly 70 million accounts have been created thus far, the White House reported last month, though that’s largely a result of a change by the Treasury to allow for automatic enrollment. Musk’s matching donation will come later, he remarked on X, sometime after mid-June 2027. That’s when a 366-day lockup expires that he agreed to as part of the SpaceX initial public offering earlier this year. The Starbase, Texas-based company noted that Gwynne Shotwell, its president and chief operating officer, previously pledged with her husband to donate more than 2 million shares to Trump accounts. But there are strict eligibility requirements associated with those donations, which parents can check online. Combined, the gifts from the company, Musk, and Shotwell could have a value of more than $18 billion given the stock’s current price and if all eligible Trump accounts have been claimed. These donations also do something that’s delving into new territory: They guarantee that potentially millions of Americans will become long-term shareholders of SpaceX. YOU GET A STOCK! Just as Oprah famously announced a new car to every person in her studio audience back in the early 2000s, Musk and other billionaires are saying the same to kids now: “You get a stock!” But that could create a conundrum of sorts for parents as more and more money is likely to flow into these accounts from billionaires. The Treasury recently implemented new rules that allow companies and other donors to gift individual stocks to these accounts, while also limiting trading activity in them, as The Wall Street Journal reported. Children and their parents can neither pick nor reject stocks that are donated to a child’s account—and they can’t sell them for five years. And yet, there’s free money on the line. If parents don’t claim an account on behalf of their kid, their kid misses out on a potentially lucrative portfolio. Despite the move to automatic enrollment, some manual steps are still required, which means parents need to claim an account by downloading an app from the Trump accounts website. Musk couldn’t help but tout the prospects of what that could mean to millions of prospective shareholders—something that resonated with investors, too, as the stock has jumped nearly 5% in the past two days of trading. “If SpaceX succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun’s energy, it will be worth about a million times the current global economy,” Musk posted. “These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them. I recommend holding on to your shares.”.

The Starbase, Texas-based manufacturer noted that Gwynne Shotwell, its president and chief operating officer, previously pledged with her husband to donate more than 2 million shares to Trump accounts. But there are strict eligibility requirements associated with those donations, which parents can check online.

Combined, the gifts from the organization, Musk, and Shotwell could have a value of more than $18 billion given the stock’s current price and if all eligible Trump accounts have been claimed. These donations also do something that’s delving into new territory: They guarantee that potentially millions of Americans will become long-term shareholders of SpaceX.

Just as Oprah famously announced a latest car to every person in her studio audience back in the early 2000s, Musk and other billionaires are saying the same to kids now: “You get a stock!”.

But that could create a conundrum of sorts for parents as more and more money is likely to flow into these accounts from billionaires.

It has been revealed that the Treasury recently implemented upcoming rules that allow companies and other donors to gift individual stocks to these accounts, while also limiting trading activity in them, as The Wall Street Journal reported. Children and their parents can neither pick nor reject stocks that are donated to a child’s account—and they can’t sell them for five years.

Sources indicate that and yet, there’s free money on the line. If parents don’t claim an account on behalf of their kid, their kid misses out on a potentially lucrative portfolio. Despite the move to automatic enrollment, some manual steps are still required, which means parents need to claim an account by downloading an app from the Trump accounts website.

Musk couldn’t help but tout the prospects of what that could mean to millions of prospective shareholders—something that resonated with investors, too, as the stock has jumped nearly 5% in the past two days of trading.

According to recent reports, “If SpaceX succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun’s energy, it will be worth about a million times the current global economy,” Musk posted. “These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them. I recommend holding on to your shares.”.

The Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard 2

📅 10 Feb 2025 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2065 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Hugging Face

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the growing availability of LLMs supporting Arabic, both as monolingual and multilingual models, prompted the community to create dedicated Arabic language leaderboards.
  • While these approaches helped spark initial interest in Arabic benchmarking, they also introduced several challenges:.
  • Recent findings suggest that these limitations underscore the need for a more unified, accessible, and transparent benchmarking platform—one that not only enables but encourages genuine and reproducible experimentation for the entire Arabic NLP community.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the growing availability of LLMs supporting Arabic, both as monolingual and multilingual models, prompted the community to create dedicated Arabic language leaderboards. Previously, Arabic-focused leaderboards were typically confined to narrow benchmarks introduced by specific authors, often as demos for their work. In these cases, the authors would set up leaderboards to demonstrate how models performed on a particular task or dataset. Alternatively, other leaderboards required owners to run evaluations on their own computing resources and then submit a JSON file containing their results for display.

While these approaches helped spark initial interest in Arabic benchmarking, they also introduced several challenges:.

Recent findings suggest that these limitations underscore the need for a more unified, accessible, and transparent benchmarking platform—one that not only enables but encourages genuine and reproducible experimentation for the entire Arabic NLP community. To address these problems, in May 2024, 2A2I, TII, and HuggingFace released the first version of the Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard - OALL [1], featuring 14 benchmarks across a wide range of tasks including reading comprehension, sentiment analysis, and question answering among others.

In September 2024, a collaboration between SDAIA and the King Salman Global Academy for Arabic Language introduced the Balsam Index, which includes approximately 1,400 datasets with 50,000 questions covering 67 tasks, such as grammar correction, paraphrasing, cause-and-effect classification, and text comprehension ... etc.

Later that year, on December 5th, Inception and MBZUAI announced the AraGen Leaderboard, the first generative tasks leaderboard for Arabic, introducing the 3C3H evaluation metric, which uses dynamic evaluation cycles with private test, and provides a native-Arabic and culturally-aware generative tasks dataset, AraGen Bench, to assess LLMs across four main tasks.

It has been revealed that and to end the year strong, on 19th of December 2024, Scale's Safety, Evaluations, and Alignment Lab (SEAL) published an Arabic leaderboard as part of their multilingual leaderboards. The benchmark empowering this leaderboard remains always private like all the other languages within their family of leaderboards, and relies on human-preference evaluation, using a dataset of 1,000 Arabic prompts designed to enhance chatbot interaction capabilities across complex and culturally nuanced conversations.

In less than 7 months after its launch, the first version of the Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard promptly became a vital platform for the Arabic AI community, attracting over 46,000 visitors and more than 2,000 visits in the past month (January 2025). The HuggingFace space received over 100 likes and 8 citations on Google Scholar. The community submitted more than 700 models, ranging from 1B to over 70B parameters. The submitted models originate from more than 180 unique organizations making it one of the most active LLM evaluation leaderboards. Since its launch, the leaderboard sparked numerous engaging discussions across social media, HuggingFace, Reddit, making it the most prominent Arabic leaderboard to date.

In a recent development, as depicted in Figure 1, among the ~700 models submitted to the initial version of the leaderboard, the majority are chat and finetuned models, comprising over 70%, whereas pretrained models constitute only 11%. In terms of model size, more than 50% of the models are smaller than 7B parameters.

Compared to leaderboards for other languages and as shown in Figure 2, the Open Arabic LLM leaderboard stands out as one of the most active, following closely behind the Korean, Polish, and Portuguese leaderboards, all within less than a year of its launch. Considering that Arabic is one of the most spoken languages globally, yet has relatively limited content available on the internet, these figures carry even greater significance compared to other languages.

Recent discussions within the community, including critiques of the Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard (OALL) and similar initiatives, have highlighted key shortcomings in current benchmarking practices [2]. Many researchers, developers, and language enthusiasts have emphasized the need for more direct evaluations of Arabic-specific tasks, increased transparency in how benchmarks are created, and the inclusion of more diverse datasets that reflect the breadth of Arabic dialects, domains, and real-world applications. These insights have played a central role in shaping the updated leaderboard.

The Arabic language presents unique challenges and characteristics that require specialized evaluation beyond what general NLP tasks can capture. These include intricate grammar, rich and complex morphology, the diversity of spoken dialects, and culturally nuanced safety-related considerations. A leaderboard that addresses these factors can provide a clearer picture of how well models perform in real-world Arabic language contexts.

Recent findings suggest that in the first iteration of OALL, a large portion of datasets and tasks originated from non-Arabic-speaking contexts. When adapted to Arabic, these tasks often failed to reflect real-world use cases or meet the practical needs of Arabic-speaking communities. Many tasks were direct translations from English, which frequently introduced linguistic and contextual mismatches. This approach overlooked Arabic’s unique morphological and syntactic complexities, making the tasks less effective in measuring true language understanding and modeling capabilities.

Recent findings suggest that additionally, some benchmarks from the first version of OALL became less effective over time as models achieved near-perfect scores, limiting their ability to differentiate incremental improvements. In response, the upcoming leaderboard replaces these saturated benchmarks, introducing a more relevant and up-to-date suite of evaluation tasks.

To address these gaps, the latest leaderboard incorporates tasks that are natively developed in Arabic. These tasks are designed to capture the language’s distinctive features—such as its rich morphology, subtle syntax, and context-specific usage—elements that are often lost in translation-based benchmarks. This shift ensures that evaluations are more authentic and better aligned with the realities of Arabic language use.

Furthermore, we identified a silent bug in one of the main tasks, AlGhafa, which inadvertently impacted model rankings. The glitch stemmed from a mismatch in how answer choices were checked—rather than verifying their indices, the task evaluated responses based on the choices themselves. While this was not entirely incorrect, it affected small/weak models disproportionately. Some models experienced score drops of up to 20 points, while stronger models remained relatively unaffected. This issue compromised the consistency, fairness and uniformity of the evaluations.

In reforming the leaderboard, we follow two guiding principles: remove saturated and machine translated tasks, due to inherent lower quality and possible cultural bias, and add newly available high quality native or human curated benchmarks to increase the coverage of the evaluation.

From the first version of the Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard (OALL), we keep the following benchmark datasets:.

We enrich the leaderboard by adding the following datasets, released in the past year:.

Finally, we introduce the ALRAGE benchmark: Arabic Language Retrieval Augmented Generation Evaluation. It introduces a comprehensive framework for evaluating Large Language Models' retrieval-augmented generation capabilities in Arabic. Built upon a meticulously curated dataset sourced from 40 Arabic books spanning diverse topics, from Arts & Literature to Technology & Innovation, the benchmark was created using meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B for synthetic generation and validated by native Arabic speakers with a community sprint with Argilla. The dataset structure includes questions, ground-truth answers, candidate contexts retrieved through the BAAI/bge-m3 embedding model, and target candidate indices, all designed to authentically simulate real-world RAG scenarios in Arabic.

Industry observers note that the innovative aspect of ALRAGE lies in its evaluation methodology, which implements a LLM-as-judge metric within the lighteval framework. Using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct as the judge model, the system evaluates generated responses through a structured Arabic prompt that compares the model's output against gold answers. The evaluation employs a nuanced 0-10 scoring rubric that assesses answer accuracy, relevance, and quality, with scores normalized to a 0-1 range for standardization. This technical implementation, manifested through a custom JudgeMetricWrapper class, provides a rigorous, reproducible method for evaluating Arabic language generation while maintaining sensitivity to Arabic linguistic nuances, effectively addressing the critical need for sophisticated evaluation metrics in Arabic NLP.

Table 1 summarizes the datasets kept from the first version of the leaderboard as well as the new datasets introduced in this second version.

To assess the impact of the second iteration of the Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard, we conducted a series of statistical comparisons between the two versions.

Figure 3 displays the performance scores across six benchmarks for Versions 1 and 2. Notably, ACVA and Toxigen demonstrate saturation effects at various model sizes. Alghafa in Version 1 exhibits lower saturation, which we hypothesize is due to the inclusion of both native and translated Arabic benchmarks. In contrast, the models' performance for AraTrust, ALRAGE, and Alghafa form v2 is more dispersed with respect to model size.

In a recent development, to examine the correlation between OALL and other Arabic LLM leaderboards, we compared the relative rankings of five open Arabic LLMs: google/gemma-2-27b-it, CohereForAI/aya-23-35B, CohereForAI/aya-expanse-32b, inceptionai/jais-adapted-70b-chat, and meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, across three leaderboards: OALL v2, SEAL Arabic, and AraGen. As illustrated in Figure 4, a correlation between the leaderboards is notable, with the Llama3.3-70-instruct model ranking first on both OALL v2 and AraGen, and third on SEAL. *As a clarification, AraGen at the moment only features the scores for inceptionai/jais-adapted-70b-chat, and the Arabic SEAL leaderboard only includes Jais Adapted 70B, so presumably the pretrained model. As we could not fully solve this discrepancy, we decided to evaluate inceptionai/jais-adapted-70b-chat on OALL v2 for this comparison.

To further explore the differences between the two versions of OALL, we present in Figure 5 the top models across two categories: pretrained and chat. For models submitted to OALL v1, Qwen2.5 establishes itself as a strong baseline for Arabic in all categories, particularly for pretrained models. In OALL v2, Qwen models also dominate the pretrained models category, however the Qwen/Qwen2-72B model surpasses Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B as the best pretrained/continually pretrained model, and Llama3.3-70B-instruct emerges as the leader in all categories, surpassing calme-2.1-qwen2.5-72b in performance. Overall, some model rankings have shifted in v2, while others have remained consistent. We attribute these changes to two key factors: first, the robustness of models with respect to Arabic-native benchmarks, safety, and trustworthiness; and second, the evaluation of over 700 models in OALL v1 compared to 80 models in v2, including a few recent models that might not be present in v1. We anticipate that the community will contribute to expanding the leaderboard following its release.

According to recent reports, finally, we analyzed the average scores on OALL v1 and v2 for two model families: AceGPT and Jais. As depicted in Figure 6, the trend is consistent across both versions: larger models tend to achieve higher average scores, with the exception of inceptionai/jais-family-30b-8k, that surpasses the larger inceptionai/jais-adapted-70b model on OALL v2. Overall, the average scores in v2 are higher than in v1, except for the 7B models in both families. We hypothesize that this discrepancy is due to the lower performance of smaller models on ALRAGE, as it is a generative task, which typically favors larger models.

Recent findings suggest that in this blog post, we introduced the second version of the Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard. We analyzed the existing Arabic leaderboards as well as the first version of the OALL, remarking issues such as the saturation of specific benchmarks that were removed in this second iteration. We also removed machine-translated benchmarks and retained only the Arabic native and human-translated benchmarks. Finally, we introduced upcoming benchmarks such as Aratrust, MadinaQA, native MMLU, human translated MMLU (MMLU-HT) and ALRAGE. Our goal is to offer the community an objective evaluation of Arabic LLMs, aiding in the understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of each submitted model.

Looking ahead, we hope to see the release of additional Arabic benchmarks, particularly in areas such as mathematics, reasoning, hallucination and both general and domain-specific benchmarks.

It has been revealed that the authors would like to thank Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI) for providing some of the fresh native benchmarks we are using in this version, including the new MMLU-HT dataset. We also extend our gratitude to TII for their generous sponsorship of the inference hardware needed for the evaluation backend. We also thank our friends at Hugging Face for their continuous support and being always 🤗 whenever needed. Thanks to all people focusing on evaluation and leaderboards for their languages and tasks. Lastly, we thank the community for their engagement and valuable feedback on the first version of the OALL. Looking forward to seeing many models on the leaderboard 🚀.

A popular password manager was hacked. Here’s what you need to know

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that password managers are the safest way short of secret sticky notes to keep track of the hundreds of logins in your life, but even they don’t have perfect security.
  • Password managers are the safest way short of secret sticky notes to keep track of the hundreds of logins in your life, but even they don’t have perfect security.
  • It has been revealed that popular Password manager 1Password disclosed this week that hackers breached its systems this month and accessed the software’s source code.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that password managers are the safest way short of secret sticky notes to keep track of the hundreds of logins in your life, but even they don’t have perfect security. Popular Password manager 1Password disclosed this week that hackers breached its systems this month and accessed the software’s source code. While no breach is good news, the attackers were not able to access 1Password users’ most sensitive data, including their passwords, secret keys, and information stored in user vaults. “At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker,” the company emphasized in a blog post on the incident. The security of the software maker’s apps and browser extensions was also not affected by the breach. The attackers were able to burrow into 1Password’s system after gaining access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. By pushing malicious code into its backend systems, the attackers made off with administrative data on a subset of 1Password customers, including customer names, email addresses, and “non-secret internal metadata” about accounts. Anyone who uses 1Password doesn’t need to take extra steps right now, but they should be extra vigilant for phishing attempts in the future. That includes being skeptical of “unexpected emails, texts or calls that mention 1Password, invitations, or account recovery attempts,” according to the company. The password manager will never ask its customers for an account password or a secret key. In response, 1Password states that it has disabled the compromised GitHub account, rotated and revoked exposed internal credentials, and brought in external cybersecurity experts to advise the software maker on its response, among other measures. Security for everybody The world of cybersecurity moves fast – and now that cycle is speeding up even in light of AI. Security companies are leveraging artificial intelligence to detect threats at the same time that malicious actors are putting it to work cracking into accounts at scale. 1Password CTO Nancy Wang described the unique challenges and opportunities the company faces in light of widespread AI adoption in a recent interview with Fast Company. While a sea of vibe-coded apps have introduced security holes human software makers would have caught, AI can also scan massive chunks of code for vulnerabilities. “AI’s been a mixed bag, just because that work has been so gnarly and technical,” Wang said. Aside from the millions of people who rely on 1Password, more than 200,000 businesses use the password manager to keep track of their credentials. That number includes nearly a third of the largest companies in the U.S., according to 1Password. Fast Company named the software maker to its 2025 list of Brands That Matter for its user-friendly approach to security. “1Password was built on the belief that security should be accessible to everyone,” 1Password CEO David Faugno said last year. “In an industry that too often leads with fear and complexity, we’ve built our foundation on trust, usability, and the human experience.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanksgiving may be over, but one of the holiday’s biggest traditions is still to come. For the first time in its history, the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is taking place on a day other than Thanksgiving. On Wednesday, Macy’s, NBC, and Fresh York City officials made the unprecedented decision to postpone the parade until Saturday, November 28, after forecasts called for dangerous winds, heavy rain, and coastal flooding. While the parade was canceled from 1942 through 1944 during World War II, weather has never before forced organizers to move the event to another day. The timing is particularly noteworthy given that this year marks the parade’s 100th edition, a milestone Macy’s is celebrating with an expanded lineup of balloons, floats, musical performances, and celebrity appearances. NBC aired a replay of the 2025 parade on Thanksgiving morning instead. The live celebration will take place Saturday, although the last-minute schedule change has forced some performers to adjust their looks. Here’s what to expect from the rescheduled parade and how to watch it. Who is performing at the 2026 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade? Savannah Guthrie, Hoda Kotb, and Al Roker are slated to return as hosts of NBC’s broadcast. The originally revealed musical lineup includes RAYE, Teddy Swims, Megan Moroney, Natasha Bedingfield, Queen Latifah, Jimmy Fallon and The Roots, JoJo, Smash Mouth, and Keke Palmer, among others. A special Broadway performance featuring a 10-minute medley from nine musicals, including Hamilton, Wicked, and Rent, is still expected to take place. The Radio City Rockettes are also on the announced lineup. However, not everyone who planned to participate on Thursday will be able to stick around for Saturday. The University of Alabama’s Million Dollar Band, for instance, is returning home to perform at Saturday’s Iron Bowl football game. Macy’s Great American Marching Band is also unable to participate in the rescheduled event. Other groups have turned to crowdfunding to cover the unexpected cost of extending their stays in New York. A high school marching band from Pearland, Texas, raised $350,000 in less than 24 hours to enable more than 500 students and staff members to stay for the parade. How to watch the 2026 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade The rescheduled parade will step off at 8:30 a.m. ET on Saturday, November 28, and is expected to conclude around noon. NBC will televise the parade, while cord-cutters can stream it on Peacock. A Spanish-language broadcast will also be available on Telemundo. Viewers with live TV streaming subscriptions that carry NBC, including YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV, and Fubo, can also tune in. If you’d rather sleep in on Saturday morning, NBC is scheduled to air an encore presentation at 2 p.m. ET/PT.

Google Maps is rolling out an revision on Android Auto that provides better navigation routes specifically for motorcycles.

Owners in India have recently noticed that Google Maps for Android Auto is showing a new message asking them to restart the app to “switch to two-wheeler directions.” Once enabled, a motorcycle icon appears on the ETA card.

On a support page, Google details this mode, explaining that the mode tailors directions to skip routes where two-wheelers are not allowed, while also included narrow roads that may be faster. Google states that the feature is only available in “limited locations.”.

Industry observers note that these directions show you routes away from roads where two-wheelers aren’t allowed. You may be directed towards shortcuts along narrower side roads.

Sources indicate that the page also explains that it is only available for mobile devices, with no mention of Android Auto and CarPlay. Yet, a number of owners are seeing the adjustment on their devices within the past two weeks, so it seems Google is expanding it out to Android Auto. That makes sense, as Android Auto has been working to better accommodate motorcycles for a while, and some motorcycles even now have Android Auto support built-in.
